clue.text: Naval front line to keep moving about

blocks.note: the prow is the front of a ship
L is the usual abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Warships at the front line are told to keep moving to stay safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to roam restlessly around an area, often looking for prey or trouble.

clue.text: Rather solemn youngster in online ad

blocks.note: po-faced means solemn and disapproving; 'rather' takes just a part of that word
a pup is a young dog, or a cheeky young person

explanation.surface: A serious-looking child appears in an internet advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is the start of po-faced, a British word for humourlessly solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up is an advertising window that springs open unbidden while browsing a website.

clue.text: Clear dispute about Henry's cricketing blunder

blocks.note: overt means plain, open, clear to see
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A plain-spoken argument about Henry's mistake on the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: The dispute is 'about' Henry in the sense of attached to him, so it follows the H.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an overthrow is a wild return by a fielder that lets the batters take extra runs, a fielding error.

clue.text: Refuse to consider some fun, having nowhere to play tennis?

blocks.note: a laugh is a bit of fun
without a court, a tennis player is literally out of court

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to join in the fun because no tennis court is free.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a legal idiom; the wordplay takes it literally, as a laugh plus a tennis player with no court.
explanation.definitionFit: To laugh something out of court is to dismiss it as too ridiculous for serious attention.

clue.text: Baffled guy about Channel Islands' architectural style

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: 'you've got me' means you have baffled me
a guy is a man, referred to as him
CI is the abbreviation for Channel Islands, with the possessive supplying S

explanation.surface: A man is puzzled by the architectural style of buildings on Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You've got me' is what a baffled person says, so baffled the guy reads as two pieces; the possessive gives the Channel Islands an extra S.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothicism is the use or imitation of the Gothic style, with pointed arches and tracery.

clue.text: Suppose visitors to be out of time

indicators.note: something that is out of the word has been removed from it

blocks.note: guests are visitors
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: We assume our visitors have run out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of GUESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to suppose or conjecture without sure knowledge.

clue.text: Internal manoeuvres swamping Italy every thousand days roughly

indicators.note: to swamp something is to engulf it, so one piece surrounds the other
manoeuvres are moves and repositionings, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Political manoeuvring inside Italy flares up every three years or so.
explanation.walkthrough: Three years is about 1,096 days, hence 'roughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial means happening once every three years, which is a little over a thousand days.

clue.text: Popular tune - claim disc misrepresented original theatrical version?

indicators.note: something misrepresented is distorted, so these letters are shown in a new order

blocks.note: in means fashionable, popular
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hit song's maker claims the record misrepresents the stage show's original score.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: this is music written for a play rather than a version of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental music is the score composed to accompany a stage production, its original setting.

clue.text: Writer that is penning nonsense, note

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as sheep are penned

blocks.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
BS is slang shorthand for nonsense
N abbreviates note

explanation.surface: A writer is caught scribbling rubbish in a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' tempts you toward a pen; here it is a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Writer – uplifting stuff – anxious to include supposedly standard speech

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means reading the word from bottom to top
to include something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
keen means eager, anxious to do something
RP is Received Pronunciation, the accent once treated as standard British English

explanation.surface: A writer of inspiring material is keen to use proper standard English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supposedly' hints that Received Pronunciation's claim to be standard is debatable; it was the accent of BBC newsreaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker pen is a felt-tipped pen with a broad point, a writing implement.

clue.text: Piano runs are frustrating in Chopin piece?

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
R abbreviates runs in cricket scoring
to elude is to baffle or evade, as an answer eludes you

explanation.surface: A pianist finds the fast runs in a Chopin work frustrating.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Chopin wrote a famous set of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin's 24 Preludes, Op. 28, are short piano pieces, so a prelude is an example of his work.

clue.text: Not a canine? Man with this could create Canis Minor!

indicators.note: creating something new from given material means rearranging its letters
with this says the answer joins the other word, so taking that word back out of the result leaves the answer

blocks.note: taken as written; the constellation of the Little Dog
these three letters are what the answer lacks to make the constellation

explanation.surface: A dog-related joke: a man plus something rearranged yields the Little Dog constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: MAN with the answer rearranges to CANIS MINOR, so the answer is CANIS MINOR minus the letters of MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisors and canines are different kinds of teeth, so an incisor is a tooth that is not a canine.

clue.text: Hot and cold water source returned for repair

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the whole run is read backwards

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap
C for cold, as on a tap
a tap supplies water

explanation.surface: A mixer tap is sent back to be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a piece of material put over a hole to mend it, so a patch is a repair.

clue.text: Limitations of sound expert restricting new variety entertainment?

indicators.note: restricting something means hemming it in on both sides

blocks.note: the edges of the word sound are S and D, written out in full
an ace is an expert
N abbreviates new

explanation.surface: An expert in sound limits a new kind of variety act.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters are read as the phrase S AND D. The sand dance is a comic music-hall routine, made famous by Wilson, Keppel and Betty, done in Egyptian costume on sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand dance is a soft-shoe routine on a sanded stage, a classic British variety-theatre turn.

clue.text: Little sound from those delivering aerobatic display?

definitions.text: Little sound from those delivering aerobatic display?

blocks.clueFragment: Little sound from those delivering aerobatic display?
blocks.note: surface reading: a quiet noise made by a team of stunt pilots

blocks.clueFragment: Little sound from those delivering aerobatic display?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the swirling flock of starlings, named for the soft whirring noise of their wings

explanation.walkthrough: Aerobatic display suggests the Red Arrows, but the performers are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for a huge swooping flock of starlings comes from the low murmur of their wingbeats.

clue.text: Pope modified line when among simple marine folk

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters change their order
among means placed in the middle of, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
L abbreviates line
mere means simple, nothing more than

explanation.surface: The Pope adjusts a line of teaching when he is among humble fishing folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Merpeople are the mythical mermaids and mermen living in the sea.

clue.text: Cheap tyre burst for example

indicators.note: a burst object is blown apart, so these letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A budget tyre blowing out is held up as a cautionary instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is a perfect or typical specimen of something, the model example.

clue.text: Suggestion King should abandon foreign visit?

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so it drops out

blocks.note: R stands for Rex, king
a trip is a journey, here one abroad

explanation.surface: An adviser proposes the monarch cancel a state visit abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a piece of useful advice or a hint, a suggestion.

clue.text: Top figures university brought in to cut back a lot of green

indicators.note: something brought in is put inside another piece
a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter goes
back means at the rear, so this piece is attached behind the first

blocks.note: to trim is to cut
U abbreviates university
virid is a literary word for green

explanation.surface: Leading academics have a university brought in to cut back greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: Triumviri is the Latin plural of triumvir; 'back' is not a reversal here but places the green piece at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumviri were the three men sharing power in a Roman triumvirate, the leading figures of state.

clue.text: Crude strength when stripped?

indicators.note: stripped means peeled bare, so the outer layer of letters comes off

blocks.note: brawn is physical strength

explanation.surface: Raw strength on show when someone takes their shirt off.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose the first and last letters of BRAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw means unrefined or unprocessed, the same sense as crude oil or crude sugar.

clue.text: Mystic helping to obscure start of regular astronomical event

indicators.note: to obscure something is to hide it from view, so that letter disappears
'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'regular'

blocks.note: occult means mystic, supernatural
a ration is a portion or helping
the first letter of regular

explanation.surface: A mystic helps to hide the beginning of a recurring event in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: RATION loses its R, the start of regular.
explanation.definitionFit: An occultation is when one celestial body passes in front of and hides another, as the moon hides a star.

clue.text: Productive compound in effect must include iodine

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside
a compound is a mixture, so these letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemist says a productive compound must contain iodine to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficient means achieving maximum output with little waste, so productive in a useful way.

clue.text: Features limiting Republican debacle

indicators.note: limiting something means bounding it on each side

blocks.note: your face is your features
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: Commentators' faces show contempt at the Republican fiasco.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is an absurd, chaotic event, the sort of shambles also called a debacle.

clue.text: Stirs black powder up around diamonds

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another
in a down clue going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: soot is a black powder left by burning
D abbreviates diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: Someone stirs black powder up and finds diamonds within.
explanation.walkthrough: SOOT is reversed and D sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To-dos are commotions or fusses, the same sense as stirs in 'cause a stir'.

clue.text: Old woman satisfied US playwright

blocks.note: ma is a mother, an informal old woman
met means fulfilled, as in met the demand

explanation.surface: An elderly lady is pleased with an American dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: David Mamet is the American dramatist of Glengarry Glen Ross and Oleanna.

clue.text: Weight lifting record broken by right fool

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means raising the letters so they read upwards
something broken by another piece has that piece wedged inside it

blocks.note: WT is the abbreviation for weight
an EP is an extended-play record
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A weightlifting record is broken by some idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weight lifting' looks like one sport, but the weight abbreviation is what gets lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, a fool.

clue.text: One-third of judges tucking into booze? It's bad for the case

indicators.note: one-third of a six-letter word is its first two letters
tucking into means getting inside something

blocks.note: perry is an alcoholic drink made from pears
the first two of the six letters

explanation.surface: Judges drinking on the job would harm the case they are hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry is a pear cider, the pear version of the apple drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury, lying under oath, is a crime that badly damages a court case.

clue.text: Think little of reckless speeds around island

indicators.note: reckless means wild and uncontrolled, so these letters are thrown about
around means surrounding one piece with another

blocks.note: taken as written
I abbreviates island

explanation.surface: Someone has a low opinion of reckless driving round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To despise someone is to feel contempt for them, to hold them in low regard.

clue.text: Recent upset? Diminished, losing initial upright character

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so these letters land in a new order
losing its initial means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
less means reduced, diminished

explanation.surface: A recent setback has worn down someone's moral backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: LESS loses its L to leave ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Erectness is the quality of standing straight, an upright bearing.

clue.text: Felon taking piano and flute

blocks.note: crim is slang for criminal
p is the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: A criminal picks up a piano and a flute.
explanation.walkthrough: Flute here is a verb, to make grooves or folds, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to press small ridges or folds into material, which is what fluting does too.
